input_signals.name: Capitalized Intangible Yield x Intensity
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5)))), IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with high operating yield on a capitalized intangible asset base and high accumulated intangible investment intensity earn higher future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The first component adds back R&D and advertising and scales profitability by book assets plus a recent intangible-investment stock. Multiplying by accumulated intangible intensity emphasizes firms where accounting understatement of productive assets should be economically material.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( add( oibdp, add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ) ), add( at, ts_sum( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), 5 ) ) ) ), ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), 5 ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Productive Intangible Overhead
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, xsga)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), xsga)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose SG&A is more explicitly intangible-investment-oriented and produces high operating profit per SG&A dollar earn higher future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: SG&A can mix maintenance overhead with productive intangible creation, so the intangible share of SG&A helps identify higher-quality overhead. The profitability-per-SG&A component validates that the intangible-heavy expense base is already generating operating returns.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oibdp, xsga ) ), ind_rank( ratio( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), xsga ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Funded Intangible Compounder
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 3), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with sustained operating cash-flow profitability and meaningful recent intangible investment earn higher future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Operating cash flow provides a cleaner validation that intangible spending is funded by productive operations rather than external financing or accounting accruals. The accumulated R&D-plus-advertising leg captures a recent intangible investment base while avoiding an unstable single-year expense spike.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), 3 ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Durable Intangible Profitability
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5), at)), MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with large cumulative intangible investment, sustained profitability, and low profitability volatility earn higher future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Productive intangible assets should generate durable earnings power, not just a one-period profitability spike. The interaction rewards firms where cumulative R&D and advertising are accompanied by both high and stable operating profitability, consistent with an underrecognized intangible moat.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), 5 ), at ) ), mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oibdp, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( neg( vol( ratio( oibdp, at ), 5 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Signed Intangible Profit Validation
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(MUL(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(ADD(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5), COALESCE(SUB(intan, COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), 0)), at)), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms earn higher future returns when a large intangible asset base is paired with positive current operating profitability.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the masked profitability sort with a signed interaction: high values require both profitability and intangible capital, while unprofitable intangible-heavy firms become explicitly low rather than arbitrary. Using cumulative R&D and advertising plus identifiable non-goodwill intangibles also reduces dependence on a single zero-heavy R&D reporting channel.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( mul( ratio( oibdp, at ), ratio( add( ts_sum( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), 5 ), coalesce( sub( intan, coalesce( gdwl, 0 ) ), 0 ) ), at ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Lagged Intangible Margin Inflection
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 1), 1)), IND_RANK(LAG(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 3), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with prior intangible investment followed by improving operating margins are more likely to have productive intangible capital.
input_signals.reasoning: This shifts the mechanism from contemporaneous sales-growth scaling to a time-sequenced payoff test: past R&D and advertising should show up in subsequent margin improvement. It avoids division by intangible intensity and does not reward firms merely for having near-zero R&D or advertising.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( delta( ratio( oibdp, sale ), 1 ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( lag( ratio( ts_sum( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), 3 ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Intangible Profitability Acceleration
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(ACCEL(RATIO(oibdp, at))), IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 3), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Intangible-intensive firms with accelerating operating profitability earn higher future returns as intangible investments become economically validated.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids a static low-profitability short by focusing on improvement in profitability rather than simply rewarding or penalizing the profitability level. The positive sign is consistent with markets underreacting when intangible-heavy firms begin converting investment into operating results.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( accel( ratio( oibdp, at ) ) ), ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), 3 ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Intangible Harvest Operating Leverage
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(LAG(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 3), at), 1)), MUL(IND_RANK(TREND(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), sale), 3)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with prior intangible investment, improving operating margins, and easing intangible expense intensity are entering a profitable harvest phase.
input_signals.reasoning: This tests whether past R&D and advertising are beginning to scale, rather than simply rewarding current high spending. The margin-trend leg validates productivity, while the declining spending-intensity trend captures operating leverage from previously built intangible assets.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( lag( ratio( ts_sum( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), 3 ), at ), 1 ) ), mul( ind_rank( trend( ratio( oibdp, sale ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( neg( trend( ratio( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), sale ), 3 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Internal Intangibles over Goodwill Profit
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), IND_RANK(SUB(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5), at), RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Profitable firms with internally built intangible investment rather than acquisition goodwill earn higher future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Internally generated R&D and advertising are more likely to be understated by accounting, while goodwill may reflect acquisition premia already paid. The interaction rewards profitability when it is paired with internal intangible formation and penalizes goodwill-heavy profitability that is less clearly an underrecognized productive asset base.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), ind_rank( sub( ratio( ts_sum( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), 5 ), at ), ratio( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Gross-to-Operating Intangible Conversion
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(TREND(RATIO(oibdp, SUB(revt, cogs)), 3), 1)), IND_RANK(LAG(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 3), sale), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose prior intangible investment is followed by better conversion of gross profit into operating profit earn higher future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids the DuPont margin-times-turnover collapse by measuring operating drop-through from gross profit rather than asset turnover. The interaction tests whether R&D and advertising create scalable products or brands whose gross profits increasingly survive operating-expense absorption.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( trend( ratio( oibdp, sub( revt, cogs ) ), 3 ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( lag( ratio( ts_sum( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), 3 ), sale ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Validated Intangible Turnover Improvement
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, sale), 3)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(sale, ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 3))), 1), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with strong cash margins and improving sales generation on an intangible-adjusted asset base earn higher future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The adjusted turnover change tests whether reported assets plus recent intangible investment are becoming more productive, while cash margin validates that the sales efficiency is not low-quality revenue. This shifts away from a pure profitability-level × intangible-intensity double sort toward improvement in the productivity of the broader asset base.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oancf, sale ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( winsor( delta( ratio( sale, add( at, ts_sum( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), 3 ) ) ), 1 ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Profitable Intangible Reinvestment Share
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), sale), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), ADD(oibdp, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)))), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with strong pre-intangible operating profitability that reinvest a meaningful share of that surplus into R&D and advertising earn higher future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This moves away from the volatility-of-spend variant by asking whether intangible investment is funded out of a current economic surplus. The second leg is a reinvestment share of pre-intangible profit rather than raw intangible intensity, so the signal targets productive reinvestment capacity instead of a generic profitability-level × intangible-stock interaction.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( add( oibdp, add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ) ), sale ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), add( oibdp, add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ) ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Intangible Gross-Margin Upgrade
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt), 1), 1)), MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 1)), IND_RANK(LAG(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 3), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with prior intangible investment, current operating profitability, and improving gross margins earn higher future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This changes the drop-through idea into a product-differentiation or production-efficiency mechanism: successful intangibles should raise gross margin through pricing power, better products, or lower delivery costs. The operating-margin leg requires that the gross-margin improvement is already reaching operating profitability rather than remaining an isolated revenue-cost effect.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( delta( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), revt ), 1 ), 1 ) ), mul( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( oibdp, sale ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( lag( ratio( ts_sum( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), 3 ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Lagged Intangible Profit Dollar Payoff
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(oibdp, 1), at), 1)), IND_RANK(LAG(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 3), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose prior intangible investment is followed by an increase in operating profit dollars relative to assets earn higher future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This is not a denominator tweak to margin inflection; it tests whether prior R&D and advertising translate into absolute operating-profit expansion rather than merely improved sales-scaled margins. Scaling the profit change by assets preserves broad coverage and avoids rewarding near-zero intangible spenders through an unstable profit-per-intangible denominator.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( delta( oibdp, 1 ), at ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( lag( ratio( ts_sum( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), 3 ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Profitable Intangible Investment Mix
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(MUL(RATIO(oibdp, sale), COALESCE(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 3), ADD(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 3), ABS(DELTA(at, 1)))), 0)), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose investment mix is dominated by expensed intangibles rather than balance-sheet asset accumulation, and that are already operating-profitable, earn higher future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This repairs the scale problem by comparing dollar intangible investment to dollar asset accumulation, rather than subtracting an investment-intensity level from an asset-growth rate. The signed profitability interaction makes non-investing firms neutral and focuses the long leg on profitable firms where accounting is most likely to understate productive asset formation.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( mul( ratio( oibdp, sale ), coalesce( ratio( ts_sum( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), 3 ), add( ts_sum( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), 3 ), abs( delta( at, 1 ) ) ) ), 0 ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Intangible Expense Productivity Mix
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(MUL(COALESCE(RATIO(oibdp, ADD(dp, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)))), 0), COALESCE(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), ADD(dp, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)))), 0)), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose productive expense base is more intangible than depreciating physical capital, and that generate high operating profit per dollar of that base, earn higher future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This moves away from gross-profit dollar recombinations and tests a different accounting channel: expensed intangible investment versus depreciated tangible capital. High values require both an intangible-heavy investment-expense mix and realized operating profit productivity from that mix.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( mul( coalesce( ratio( oibdp, add( dp, add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ) ) ), 0 ), coalesce( ratio( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), add( dp, add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ) ) ), 0 ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Expensed Intangible Recognition Gap
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), sale), RATIO(DELTA(COALESCE(SUB(intan, COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), 0), 1), sale)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Profitable firms whose internal intangible investment is expensed rather than recognized as balance-sheet intangible asset growth earn higher future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The second leg compares two flow-scaled quantities: current expensed R&D/advertising intensity versus the change in identifiable non-goodwill intangible assets. High values identify profitable firms where accounting is most likely understating internally generated productive capital.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( oibdp, sale ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( winsor( sub( ratio( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), sale ), ratio( delta( coalesce( sub( intan, coalesce( gdwl, 0 ) ), 0 ), 1 ), sale ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Intangible Cash Dropthrough
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(LAG(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 3), at), 1)), MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(oancf, sale), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(DELTA(oancf, 1), at), RATIO(DELTA(sale, 1), at)), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with prior intangible investment, current cash margins, and cash-flow expansion exceeding sales expansion earn higher future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the failed self-funding/reinvestment-share construction with a cash drop-through test rather than another operating-surplus allocation ratio. The interaction asks whether past R&D and advertising are producing incremental cash economics beyond simple revenue growth.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( lag( ratio( ts_sum( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), 3 ), at ), 1 ) ), mul( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( oancf, sale ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( winsor( sub( ratio( delta( oancf, 1 ), at ), ratio( delta( sale, 1 ), at ) ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Intangible Overhead Discipline
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 1)), MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), sale), 3), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(NEG(TREND(RATIO(SUB(xsga, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), sale), 3)), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Profitable firms that sustain intangible investment while reducing non-intangible SG&A overhead intensity earn higher future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids reusing the intangible-share-of-SG&A leg by explicitly separating intangible spending from residual SG&A overhead. The mechanism is overhead discipline: R&D and advertising are more credible when administrative or maintenance SG&A is being scaled down while operating margins remain positive.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( oibdp, sale ), 1 ) ), mul( ind_rank( winsor( ma( ratio( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), sale ), 3 ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( winsor( neg( trend( ratio( sub( xsga, add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ) ), sale ), 3 ) ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Profitability Outruns Intangible Spend
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5), at)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), sale), 5)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Intangible-intensive firms whose profitability is high relative to their own history beyond what is explained by a concurrent spending spike earn higher future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This decouples the profitability-rank leg from the intangible-spending leg by using reported operating margin, not an add-back margin mechanically boosted by R&D and advertising. The relative time-series spread penalizes cases where the apparent profitability signal is merely synchronized with rising intangible expense intensity.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), 5 ), at ) ), ind_rank( winsor( sub( ts_rank( ratio( oibdp, sale ), 5 ), ts_rank( ratio( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), sale ), 5 ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Intangible Demand Resilience
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 1)), MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5), at)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(sale, TS_MAX(sale, 5)), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Intangible-intensive firms with current profitability and sales near their own historical peak earn higher future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the harvest-phase duplicate with a demand-resilience mechanism rather than using lagged intensity and falling spend intensity again. Productive intangible assets should support durable customer demand, so sales remaining close to a firm’s own peak validates the intangible base alongside current profitability.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( oibdp, sale ), 1 ) ), mul( ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), 5 ), at ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sale, ts_max( sale, 5 ) ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Recognized Intangible Amortization Cash Profit
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(oancf, sale), 1)), MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(SUB(intan, COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), 0), at)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oibdp, oiadp), sale), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cash-profitable firms with identifiable non-goodwill intangibles and a large operating-income drag from depreciation or amortization earn higher future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids the expensed-gap leg that degenerates into raw R&D/advertising intensity for firms with missing intangibles. The mechanism is accounting conservatism from recognized intangible amortization: strong cash margins plus a non-goodwill intangible base suggest productive assets whose earnings are understated by noncash charges.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( oancf, sale ), 1 ) ), mul( ind_rank( ratio( coalesce( sub( intan, coalesce( gdwl, 0 ) ), 0 ), at ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( oibdp, oiadp ), sale ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Gross-Margin Floor Intangible Moat
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 1)), MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5), at)), IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Intangible-intensive firms with current operating profitability and a high worst-case gross margin over time earn higher future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the asset-turnover construction with a product-differentiation moat test. A high gross-margin floor indicates that accumulated intangible investment supports durable pricing power or product advantage, while operating profitability confirms that the moat reaches the bottom line.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( oibdp, sale ), 1 ) ), mul( ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), 5 ), at ) ), ind_rank( ts_min( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), revt ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Intangible Cost-Base Productivity
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 1)), MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), ADD(cogs, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)))), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), ADD(cogs, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)))), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with intangible-heavy value-creation costs, strong gross profit per total production-and-intangible cost, and positive operating margins earn higher future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This is not a reinvestment share of gross profit; it measures whether an intangible-heavy cost structure is producing strong product-level economics. The operating-margin leg filters for firms where gross-level intangible productivity is not offset by excessive downstream operating costs.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( oibdp, sale ), 1 ) ), mul( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), add( cogs, add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ) ) ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), add( cogs, add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ) ) ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Intangible Cash Moat Expansion

input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with prior intangible investment, durable gross-margin floors, and expanding operating cash flow earn higher future returns.
